title: Stock–Bond Correlation: Rolling 120 Sessions
revision_note: FRED's SP500 and H.15 yields are not revised after publication.
methodology: Each point is the correlation, over the trailing 120 trading sessions, between the S&P 500's daily percentage return and the daily change in the 10-year Treasury yield.

Sign convention: this compares stock returns with yield changes, and yields move opposite to bond prices. POSITIVE means stocks and yields fall together, so bond prices rise on bad stock days: the hedge is working. NEGATIVE means bond prices fall along with stocks: no hedge. Most published stock–bond correlation charts use bond returns instead, so their sign is the reverse (negative = hedge working).
notes: Above zero is the hedge working; below zero is not. The zero line is drawn.

Unpublished. FRED's SP500 is S&P Dow Jones Indices data, and S&P refused free permission to display index values on 2026-09-15 (catalog/sources/spglobal.json). This chart shows figures computed from those closes rather than the closes themselves, but the site's rule is that everything derived from S&P prices inherits the refusal, so it builds locally only (`scripts/dev.sh`).
FRED's SP500 covers only a rolling ten years, so no history before that exists here. The yields are FRED's H.15 constant-maturity series.
A day counts only if both the S&P and the Treasury yield report: the bond market is shut on some days stocks trade, so a return is measured between consecutive common dates.

presentation.summary: Rolling correlation of daily S&P 500 returns with daily 10-year yield changes. Positive = bonds are hedging stocks.
